haiku-low.q1: The API checks the replica's reports.row_count. At 10,000 rows or fewer it returns a 200 CSV download directly. Above that it returns 202 and a background job emails a link. A small export that turns out too big or too slow falls back to the 202 path.
haiku-low.q2: The unique index stops a second active export. The API returns the existing queued or running export with 202 instead, and the page shows which view it covers if the filters differ.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed signed link works for 86,400 seconds (24 hours). A bucket rule deletes the stored file after 7 days. That rule is the only cleanup; no cleanup job exists.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, with 60 s and 300 s waits. After the last failure the export is marked failed with a short error, the page shows failed, and the user is emailed a failure notice.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. All report rows and reports.row_count are read only from the replica, never the primary. The new exports table is in the primary but holds only job bookkeeping.
haiku-low.q6: In the exports table in the primary database. The page polls the status endpoint every 5 seconds while queued or running. On reopening, the page loads the user's latest exports row for that report.
haiku-low.q7: It never holds the whole file. It reads 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica and writes them into a multipart upload in 16 MiB parts, so memory stays at one buffer plus one page.
haiku-low.q8: On an exception the attempt aborts its upload. If the worker dies, the next attempt aborts the stale upload first. Nothing is visible at the key until completion, so no partial file is downloadable. The next attempt restarts from row 1.
haiku-low.q9: The page URL holds them. The click's POST sends filters and cols, which the API normalises and saves as JSON in the exports row. The job payload carries only export_id, so the handler reloads the view from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index in the database on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running'). The database rejects the second insert, so only one of two simultaneous clicks succeeds.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be complete (status done after complete_multipart), then a signed URL is generated and emailed. If rerun with status done and notified false, the job only resends the email. If notified is true, it returns without action.
haiku-low.q12: The whole CSV is built in memory before any byte is sent, so the user never gets a truncated file. A query error returns 503, nothing is stored, and the user can click again.

sonnet.q1: Step 2 reads reports.row_count from the replica. 10,000 rows or fewer: the request builds the CSV in memory and the response is 200 text/csv, saved as a download, nothing stored. Above 10,000: the API records an export and queues a background job, and the user gets 202 with {export_id, status:'queued'}. The page then shows the state, and the file comes by emailed 24-hour link. A small build falls back to the large path if it counts over 10,000 rows or takes over 40 s.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) for status queued/running rejects the insert. The API selects the existing active row and returns it with 202 {export_id, status, filters, created_at} instead of starting a second export. If its filters differ from this click, the page shows which view that export covers. If that row has no job_id and is over 2 minutes old, it is set to failed and the insert is retried.
sonnet.q3: The signed link works 24 hours, counted from when it is generated in Step 8 just before the email is sent. The file is removed by the bucket rule that deletes every object after 7 days. That rule is the only cleanup, and there is no cleanup job.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts, with 60 s and 300 s waits between them. After the last fails, on_final_failure sets status='failed' with a short error, aborts any remaining upload, and emails the user with report_export_failed. The page shows failed. This also frees the user to start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only, never the primary. The exports table is in the primary, but it holds only job bookkeeping, not report data.
sonnet.q6: In the exports table (status column: queued, running, done or failed) in the primary database. The page polls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/export/status every 5 seconds while queued or running, and stops on done or failed. It also calls this on page load, which returns the user's most recent export row, so a user who returns later sees the state. If a poll fails, the page keeps the last state and retries on the next tick.
sonnet.q7: It streams. It reads the replica with keyset paging, 5,000 rows per page, and appends CSV to one buffer. At about 16 MiB it uploads the buffer as a part of a multipart upload and empties it. Memory stays at one 16 MiB buffer plus one page, regardless of report size. A 900 MB file is about 57 parts. complete_multipart then makes the object visible. The plan says to benchmark throughput first, since 2 million rows within 30 minutes needs about 1,100 rows per second.
sonnet.q8: Nothing is downloadable, because the object appears at its key only when complete_multipart succeeds. On an exception, a finally block aborts the upload, clears upload_id and re-raises. If the worker is killed or the attempt times out, the next attempt aborts the stale upload in Step 5, and the bucket rule discards it after 24 hours. The next attempt restarts from row 1 with a new upload, because the cursor and etags live only in memory and the queue keeps no progress.
sonnet.q9: The page sends them in the POST body. The API normalises them and stores them as JSON in the filters and cols columns of the exports row in the primary database. The job payload is only {export_id}, and the handler reloads the view from the exports row.
sonnet.q10: The database, by the partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running'). One insert succeeds, and the other is rejected and returns the existing active export.
sonnet.q11: The file must be fully uploaded and complete_multipart must have succeeded, and the row must be marked done (a zero-row update is fine if another attempt already did it). Then the signed URL is generated and the email sent, and notified is set to true. If the queue runs the handler again and the row is done, the handler does not rebuild the file. If notified is false it goes to Step 8 and only sends the email. If notified is true it just returns.
sonnet.q12: The whole CSV is built in memory before any byte is sent, so the user never gets a truncated file. A query or replica error returns 503, nothing is stored, and the user can click again. If the count passes 10,000 or the time passes 40 s, it discards the buffer and falls back to the large path with a 202.
